preview.title: Try it: motor start and stop
preview.subtitle: The classic seal-in circuit. Press START and STOP and watch power flow through the rung.
preview.explanation: The motor contact, in parallel with START, keeps the circuit closed after you release the button: that is the seal-in (latch). STOP uses a normally closed contact, which opens when pressed and breaks the circuit.

scan.label: Interactive scan cycle diagram

read.name: Read inputs
read.description: The PLC copies the state of every physical input into the input image. From now until the next cycle, the program works with that copy.

execute.name: Execute program
execute.description: The program runs from top to bottom using the input image. Results are written to the output image, not to the terminals yet.

write.name: Write outputs
write.description: The output image is copied to the physical outputs: only now does the lamp turn on or off.

housekeeping.name: Diagnostics and communication
housekeeping.description: The PLC serves communications (HMI, programming device), checks its own health and resets the cycle-time watchdog. Then it starts over.

scan.hint: Flip the switch at any moment: the PLC will only notice it in the next “Read inputs” phase.

sensor.label: Wiring diagram of a three-wire sensor to a PLC input
sensor.object: Object in front of the sensor
sensor.legend: BN = brown (+24 V) · BU = blue (0 V) · BK = black (signal)
sensor.pnpOn: The PNP sensor connects the black wire to +24 V. Current enters the PLC through I0.0 and returns to 0 V through the common.
sensor.npnOn: The NPN sensor connects the black wire to 0 V. Current enters the PLC through the common from +24 V, leaves through I0.0 and flows into the sensor.
sensor.off: With no object, the sensor's internal switch is open: no current flows through the input and the PLC reads 0.

analog.label: Analog level signal simulator
analog.currentFault: 0 mA is outside the 4–20 mA range: the PLC detects the fault.
analog.voltageFault: 0 V looks like an empty tank: the fault goes unnoticed.
